Techtronics faces significant business risks in launching its new smartphone. From a market perspective, the saturated nature of the industry means intense competition for consumer attention and market share. The uncertainty surrounding consumer adoption of the unique feature poses a risk that the product may fail to differentiate itself effectively, leading to poor sales. Furthermore, the rapid innovation cycle in the mobile sector creates a risk of premature obsolescence, where the product could become outdated before it recovers its development and marketing costs.

Operationally, Techtronics must manage the risk of high inventory costs if the product does not sell quickly, as well as the potential for supply chain disruptions if demand forecasts are inaccurate. The company also risks damaging its brand reputation if the unique feature fails to meet consumer expectations or if the product is perceived as lacking in other essential areas due to the focus on a single novelty.
